answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond in a scarce, on-chain resource before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. The bond is slashed when independent audits confirm coordinated fraud, while honest agents recover it over time. This makes identities costly rather than free: an attacker creating many saffron, ember, or harbor accounts must lock up capital in each one and risks losing it, so Sybil campaigns become expensive even if account creation is cheap.
